discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, which turned Feynman's vision of a quantum simulator into a working laboratory tool. Since then, Bloch and Greiner have taken this platform further. Quantum gas microscopes resolve single atoms and spins in situ. Their experiments have revealed antiferromagnetic order, many-body localization, string order and entanglement in Hubbard systems, and they give controlled answers to questions that remain intractable in solids. Zoller's theoretical program, including artificial gauge fields, topological phases and Rydberg-based quantum computing, has guided the field throughout. This work founded modern analog quantum simulation. Today it underpins neutral-atom quantum processors worldwide and has created a new interface between atomic and condensed-matter physics.
